THE UNEVEN ICICLE CROWD: icicles hanging in an uneven crowd at very different lengths, one far longer than the rest standing well apart, each one a stack of chunky stepped pixel sides catching flat bands of pale blue and white in the cold air above

THE DENSE CLUSTER WHERE THE ROOF DIPS: a packed crowd of icicles gathered where the vault dips lowest, their chunky stepped sides pressed close together, lengths all different, the tallest leaning very slightly off-centre toward the left

THE LOW LEDGE SCATTER: a scatter of short stubby icicles along a low ledge, each one a different width and height, their hard pixel edges catching a flat band of white at the tip and blue above, scattered along the ice shelf where they grew

THE CHANDELIER CLUSTER: a chandelier cluster of icicles hanging over the open floor, the longest drop at the front left of the group with five shorter ones behind it stepping up in uneven intervals, their chunky stepped sides pale at the top and deep blue toward the points

THE ORGAN-PIPE FALL: a frozen fall standing in rounded ranks of uneven height like the pipes of a great organ, their stepped blocky sides pale at the front and deep blue in the hollows behind, the tallest rank set well to the right of centre

THE HEAVY PLEATED WALL FOLD: a hanging fold of ice down one wall in soft heavy pleats, each pleat a stack of chunky stepped pixel bands of white and pale blue, the folds deeper on the left side and shallower where they thin toward the floor

THE ROUNDED CASCADE: a frozen cascade stepping down in rounded shelves, each shelf a blocky pixel ledge rimmed in white, the drop between them different at every step, the lowest shelf jutting out farther to one side than the others

THE HALF-SHADOW CURTAIN: a wide fold of ice with its left half sitting deep in blue shadow and its right edges catching hard pixel bands of bright white, the pleats uneven in width across the face, the hem ragged and stepped at the bottom

THE STEPPED CLEAR POOLS: three shelves of impossibly clear meltwater stepping down, each rimmed with a scalloped white lip in chunky pixel steps, the lowest wide and glassy still and set well off to the left side of the floor

THE SCALLOPED RIM POOL: a rimmed pool of meltwater with a scalloped white lip built up in blocky stepped pixel bands, the rim thicker on the near side and thinner at the far left, the water inside showing flat bands of pale blue and clear white

THE BLUE BASIN: a shallow basin of soft blue water set into the floor off to one side, its edges stepped in chunky pixel blocks of white and pale blue ice, the water sitting perfectly still with a flat band of deep blue at its centre

THE STEPPING POOL CHAIN: a chain of small pools of different sizes stepping away across the floor, each one a different shape and depth, connected by thin runnels of clear water, the smallest pool set farthest off to the right and almost round

THE STRIDING ARCH: a natural arch of ice striding over a dark gap, its two feet planted at different heights on the floor, its crown slightly off-centre, the underside built in chunky stepped pixel blocks of pale blue shading to white at the highest point

THE ROPE-LINE BRIDGE: a narrow bridge of ice crossing from one ledge to another, one old frozen rope handline running along its right side fixed at uneven intervals, the bridge surface stepped in blocky pixel bands of blue-white and thicker at one end than the other

THE THIN-SPANNED ARCH: a low span of ice worn thin toward the middle, the thinned section built in flat stepped pixel bands of pale blue so pale they are almost white, the span thicker on the left foot and set at a slight angle across the gap

THE CORNER STAIR: steps worn into the ice climbing one corner, each step a different depth and height, their edges hard stepped pixel blocks of white over blue, the highest step set well to the left and jutting out slightly farther than the ones below

THE RUNNING RAMP: a wide ramp of ice running down to a lower floor, its surface built in wide flat pixel bands of pale blue growing darker toward the bottom, the left edge higher than the right so the ramp tilts gently across its width

THE BLOCKY WALL LEDGES: a set of blocky ice ledges stepping up one wall at uneven heights, each ledge a different width and depth built in hard pixel steps of white and blue, the highest ledge set to the right and protruding farthest from the wall

THE SAGGING BAND WALL: walls layered in flat bands of blue and white that sag and bend around a bulge on the right side, the bands closer together above the bulge and spread wide below it, every band a hand-placed row of chunky stepped pixel colour

THE TILTED OLD BANDS: a section of wall where old bands of pale blue and white run at a tilt across the face, each band a flat pixel stripe laid at a slightly different angle from the one below, the tilt steepening toward the upper right corner

THE DEEP-BANDED CLEAR WALL: a wall of clear ice with white bands reaching deep into it, each band visible as a flat pixel stripe fading from bright white at the surface to pale blue far inside, the bands spaced unevenly and bending very slightly downward at the left

THE STANDING PILLAR: a thick pillar of ice standing where a frozen fall met the floor, its sides built in chunky stepped pixel bands of white and pale blue, the pillar slightly wider at the base and set well to the right of centre on the cave floor

THE THREE SPIRES: three ice spires of different heights, the tallest and middle one standing close together on the left, the smallest standing well apart to the right, each spire a stack of blocky stepped pixel bands narrowing to a blunt tip of flat white

THE CLEAR CRACKED FLOOR: a floor of clear blue-black ice with white cracks reaching across it in branching pixel lines, the cracks thicker on the left side and thinning to single-pixel threads toward the far right, deep water showing in flat dark bands below

THE FROST FLOOR: a frost floor of untouched powder in flat bands of white and the palest blue, one drift heaped to the right side in a rounded blocky mound of stepped pixel layers, the rest of the floor flat and even in its soft banded colour
